column1: # tests/rulecheck/ledger.tsv — THE RULE-CHECKER'S LEDGER: one row per run, append-only
# tests/test_rule_checker.sh). Written by `rulecheck record` and `rulecheck resolve`
#   id              <date>-<nn>, the run dir under tests/rulecheck/runs/
#   date            the day the verdict was recorded
#   session         the 14z-N key of the sitting
#   decision        build | freeze | expectation | recommendation | calibration
#   subject         what the action is about (freeze: the expectation sets, space-separated;
#   control         the fixture PLANTED beside the real packet (calibration: the fixture itself)
#   control_verdict CAUGHT | DEAD — whether the plant's expected violation was returned
#   verdict         OK | VIOLATED | VOID (VOID when the plant was DEAD: the run licenses nothing)
#   violated        the questions VIOLATED on the real packet, or -
#   resolution      - until a VIOLATED run's stop is resolved; then one line saying what changed
#   model           the model the checker agents ran on, as given to `prepare --model`

column5: 14z-165: re-freeze the five naming/parity expectations on P2 = Demitri (the parity rigs' P2 switch, DECISIONS_HISTORY.md 14z-164b)
column10: Q4: FIXED BY WORK. The finding is correct: same_data_p2.tsv row 0x01 lists three differing Demitri chains (b:0x10, b:0x71, b:0x74) and the original p2check asserted against only b:0x71/b:0x74, leaving b:0x10 (the held-pose push box, a positional difference) neither controlled nor named. The two kinds needed different treatment, now split: b:0x71/b:0x74 are ATTACK RECORDS whose data feeds P2's compared HP, so they stay a hard NEVER (measured: Demitri never enters them on any leg of any part); b:0x10 is a POSE PUSH BOX that Demitri DOES enter legitimately (donovan_3 22 frames, donovan_12 43 frames), so a hard never was wrong. p2check gained a --report mode (name_moves.P2_REPORT=("b:0x10",), move_parity.py p2check prints "P2REPORT: b:0x10=N") and tests/audit_move_parity.sh now asserts that N is EQUAL on the native and ours legs of every part — it is (build/gates_14z165/move_parity_report.log: "holds the reported pose(s) the same on both legs"), which proves Demitri enters the pose identically on both games and its datum difference is the ONLY variable, a bounded positional confound. The claim and the frozen-expectation header now NAME b:0x10 as that confound (a candidate mechanism for the position/x DIFF rows) to be adjudicated in the family pass, not a silent gap. The .rpl inputs did not change, so the frozen expectation VALUES are unchanged; only the assertion is now complete over all three chains.
